title: Bryn Walker designer, CEO identified in fatal shooting
blurb: Bryn Walker, designer and CEO, was killed in a shooting; neighbors heard two gunshots. Witnesses reported her brother‑in‑law had mental health issues.

title: Fatal crash closes freeway lanes in Berkeley
blurb: Fatal crash closes lanes on I‑80 West near University Ave. in Berkeley, reported just before 3:30 p.m.

title: TBS turns 4 with record membership and $9K in gifts
blurb: TBS celebrates its fourth anniversary, reporting record membership and $9,000 in donations, which helped fund coverage of the fatal shooting.

title: Newsom signs law prompted by Berkeley housing projects that dodged labor standards
blurb: California Governor Newsom signed a law banning the use of the state’s density‑bonus program by large developers who bypass local labor standards.

title: Scott’s, Oakland’s unofficial boardroom, is turning 50. Meet the chefs who have made a million cioppinos
blurb: Scott’s in Oakland turns 50; three veteran chefs have worked there for nearly 40 years.

title: Update: 2 dead after shooting on Panoramic Way in Oakland
blurb: Two people died after a shooting on Panoramic Way in Oakland. Ongoing updates and photos available.

title: Tribal members saw pinyon-juniper woodlands declining. A new study confirms it.
blurb: New study confirms pinyon‑juniper woodlands in Eastern Sierra are declining, based on a three‑year collaboration among tribal nations, federal agencies, volunteers, and university researchers.

title: To decipher local laws, researchers used AI to build a database of millions of them
blurb: Researchers used AI to compile a database of millions of local ordinances, enabling easier lookup and policy analysis.

title: Berkeley after-school program expands by hundreds of kids, but staffing, transport remain a problem
blurb: Berkeley after‑school program expands by hundreds of students; staffing and transportation shortages persist, and the district projects a three‑year waitlist elimination.

title: Remembering Jack Sawyer, who founded co-ops that gave over 100 Berkeley families affordable homes to own
blurb: Jack Sawyer, co-op founder, helped over 100 Berkeley families obtain affordable homes through long-term financing, development, and advisory work.

title: The Wire: First anti-AI protester to end up in jail is a Berkeley resident

title: $7.5B plan for California science agency free from Trump’s influence will go to voters
blurb: California proposes $7.5 B bond for state science agency, free from federal influence, to offset federal research cuts, slated for 2028 ballot.

title: On complex political issues, most Americans take shortcuts to simplicity
blurb: UC Berkeley study finds many Americans simplify complex issues like immigration, climate change, and elections, avoiding deep reasoning.

title: Towering sound system named for Black folk hero John Henry comes to Berkeley library
blurb: Berkeley library installs multi‑speaker system named after John Henry, part of a week‑long music series by Derwin Deon Brown II.

title: Alborz shutters Berkeley location, Admiral Maltings announces final days, and an Emeryville food truck goes dark
blurb: Alborz closed in Berkeley; Admiral Maltings closing soon; an Emeryville food truck has shut down.

title: New UC Berkeley Journalism project will complete threatened reporters’ investigations
blurb: UC Berkeley and Forbidden Stories launch a U.S. lab to preserve threatened journalists’ investigations, partnering with a global network.

title: Dorothea Lange’s photos of Japanese American incarceration are turned immersive at OMCA
blurb: OMCA opens immersive exhibit of Dorothea Lange’s photos on 1,800 Japanese Americans forcibly removed from Oakland to camps in 1942.
